summary: The study reports on the atomic-layer deposition of Lu2O3 using a dimeric complex as the Lu source and H2O as the O source. The films are amorphous and stoichiometric, with a dielectric constant of 12±1. Annealing at 950°C in N2 leads to crystallization in the cubic bixbyite structure. The process is used to investigate Lu2O3 as a high-k dielectric material for semiconductor applications.
evidence: The Lu oxide films were deposited in an ALD F-120 ASM-microchemistry reactor on a chemical oxide covered p-type Si (100) wafer, 1–5 V cm, at 360°C. The films were found to be stoichiometric, with Lu2O3 composition, and amorphous. Annealing in nitrogen at 950°C leads to crystallization in the cubic bixbyite structure. The dielectric constant of the as-grown Lu2O3 layers is 12±1.
